dedupe_keys.name: enhancing surface cyber risk management tsa proposed rule for pipelines railroads rail transit and buses 89 fr 88488 2024

description: A notice of proposed rulemaking published by the Transportation Security Administration in the Federal Register on 7 November 2024 (docket TSA-2022-0001, RIN 1652-AA74) that would turn its post-2021 security directives into standing cyber risk management rules for surface transport. Contents: requirements for higher-risk pipeline, freight railroad, passenger railroad and rail transit owner/operators to run cyber risk management programmes in line with the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, cybersecurity incident reporting for certain over-the-road bus operators, a physical security coordinator for pipeline systems, and background on the May 2021 ransomware attack that shut 5,500 miles of East Coast fuel pipelines and on 2023 breaches at the Washington and San Francisco Bay Area transit systems. TSA estimated the rule would apply to 73 of about 620 freight railroads, 34 of about 92 public transportation agencies and passenger railroads, 71 bus operators and 115 of about 2,105 pipeline facilities, and gave ten-year cost estimates such as $881 million for passenger railroads and rail transit. Coverage: the United States, amending 49 CFR parts 1500 to 1580. Format and access: free HTML, XML and a 105-page PDF; comments closed on 5 February 2025. Licence and cost: public domain and free. Caveats: a proposal, not a final rule, and whether it was finalised was not checked. Useful for resilience and cascading failure studies that model cyber controls and incident reporting in transit and pipeline operations. It relates to the 49 CFR Part 192 and Part 195 pipeline safety regulations in the catalogue.
